item.title: PowerCut 0.9.7
item.description:
• Big takes no longer crash: a single hour-long segment with tens of thousands of words used to overflow the transcript and timeline views. Giant paragraphs now split into rows, words are lightweight, and the timeline only builds what is on screen. Scrolling and Hide Cuts are faster on every project.
  • Import a multicam or compound clip from Final Cut Pro or DaVinci Resolve (File, Import Final Cut Pro / Resolve XML, or drop the .fcpxml anywhere): the footage becomes clips with their angles and dialogue track linked.
  • Export wrappers: Plain Clips, Compound Clips For Each Clip, Compound Clip All Clips, Multicam For Each Clip, Multicam All Clips. Resolve now conforms every multicam, camera timecode and odd frame rates included.
  • The transcript follows playback (toggle next to Hide Cuts), and the Document view has Skip Cuts so only the edit plays.
  • Language: a new project starts in the language you picked last, and the first clip's speech sets the language automatically when the Whisper base model is on your Mac.
  • Background noise tolerance slider in the Pauses card; script import from Word, RTF, Markdown or text, or by dropping the file; export dialogs open in the footage folder; vertical footage exports a vertical sequence.
  • Fixes: the word context menu now always reflects the current selection and offers Favorite, Keyword and Marker on a plain word; the window reopens at the size you left it; a project that fails to open says so.

item.title: PowerCut 0.9.5
item.description:
• Chinese reads like Chinese: no more spaces between transcribed characters, in the Document view, edit popups, copied text, captions, the marker CSV and the exported .docx. Embedded English words and numbers keep their spacing, and phrase corrections typed without spaces map each character back onto its own timed word.
  • The right microphone, automatically: multi-track clips get a listen at import. Silent tracks are ruled out and the track carrying speech is chosen for transcription; close calls are marked "check mic" with each track's level and speech reading shown in the picker. Manual picks are always remembered.
  • Drop footage anywhere on the Footage panel, clip list and empty space included.
  • Fixes: Document-view word editing no longer leaks keystrokes into the page behind the popup; the background-work hint moved into the Footage column above Run Auto Edit Pass; the Footage column is a little wider.

item.title: PowerCut 0.9.4
item.description:
• Zoom in on what matters: select text in the transcript, or right-click a clip on the timeline, and punch in. Two editable preset levels, a draggable dot to aim the zoom and a ring to set the strength, live in the preview. Zooms export to Final Cut Pro and DaVinci Resolve as real transform adjustments, frame accurate and resolution independent, on plain clips, multicam and compound clips alike, and reuse your existing edit points wherever they can.
  • Copy, cut and paste text with the standard shortcuts, in both the Edit and Doc views. A blinking caret shows exactly where pasted text will land.
  • A faster app on big projects: word clicks land instantly, scrolling is smooth, Hide Cuts switches without a pause, and playback starts immediately after clicking anywhere. The transcript has a new scroll handle that tracks your drag at full speed.
  • Smaller things: the right-column panels collapse individually, the window remembers its size and position between launches, selection highlights no longer split mid-word, and annotating never pauses playback for a rebuild.

item.title: PowerCut 0.9.3
item.description:
• Six new languages in beta, filler detection included: Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Dutch, Swedish and Lithuanian. An on-device Whisper engine writes the transcript and the verbatim ear confirms every hesitation before it's cut, each language with its own filler vocabulary. First use downloads the Whisper model once (about 1.5 GB), then everything is fast and entirely local. Real clips tune these betas, so tell me how your language reads.
  • Compound clip wrapper: next to Plain clips and Multicam, exports can wrap each source in a compound clip you can open and extend in Final Cut, markers riding inside and on the timeline.
  • Listen Again for Fillers: one click in the Clean up panel runs the verbatim ear a second time and adds only what the first pass missed. Existing cuts and your restores are never touched.
  • Audio-only projects (voiceover, narration) get a timeline frame rate picker in the export bar, 23.976 through 59.94.
  • Edit and Doc now switch beside the transcript title; PowerCut says when background analysis is running instead of just feeling slower; mixed-frame-rate marker placement fixed at clip ends.

item.title: PowerCut 0.9.2
item.description:
• Frame-accurate exports: what plays in PowerCut is exactly what lands in Final Cut Pro, DaVinci Resolve, and Premiere Pro. Exports used to round every cut to the nearest frame, which could swallow a fine trim and clip a word at a cut edge that sounded perfect in PowerCut. Cuts now round outward so every exported clip fully contains what you heard: trims land exactly, words stay whole. Resolve marker EDLs, the Markers & Tags timecodes, and SRT captions all align to the exported timeline too.
  • The transcript's two faces now sit as an Edit | Doc switch right beside the title. Edit is the working surface; Doc is the clean reading page.

item.title: PowerCut 0.9.1
item.description:
• Markers, Keywords, and Favorites: press F, K, or M on any words in the transcript or Doc view, or right-click. Favorites underline green, keywords amber, markers show as teal bookmarks you can click to rename or delete. The bookmark pill in the header lists everything: click a row to jump there, export the list as a CSV or text doc with timecodes and the line each one sits on. Hide any kind, or remove all of a kind from the Edit menu. The timeline shows them too.
  • They travel with the XML: Final Cut imports keywords and favorites onto your original clips in the browser, markers land on the timeline, inside multicams, and on the source clips (struck markers stay inside the multicam only). DaVinci Resolve gets marker EDL sidecars for the timeline and each multicam, imported in two clicks. Premiere gets timeline markers.
  • Cleanup passes are now instant toggles: every pass computes in the background whether or not its box is checked, so flipping a checkbox applies or lifts it instantly. Your own edits always win, and the Run Clean ups button re-runs only what has gone stale.
  • On a Mac below macOS 26, PowerCut now says at launch that transcription needs Tahoe instead of leaving transcripts silently empty.

item.title: PowerCut 0.9.0
item.description:
• Multicam angles: give each clip its other cameras and recorders, and the export arrives in Final Cut Pro or DaVinci Resolve as one synced multicam, ready to angle-switch. Open Angles next to the Multicam wrapper option: add files, or create named blank angles and choose their clips later (blanks arrive as empty lanes). Set up once, remembered with the project.
  • Three ways to sync each angle: automatically by timecode (Sony metadata timecode in Resolve), the new Sync by audio that matches waveforms to frame accuracy using your clip's selected audio track against the angle track you pick (built for cameras with no timecode), or a manual offset in seconds.

item.title: PowerCut 0.8.4
item.description:
• Edit right on the timeline: Delete removes a selected clip (frame-accurate, even tiny slivers; in the full view it strikes and restores), C splits at the playhead, Escape clears the selection, and right-clicking a clip offers Strike, Restore, Split, Play from Here, and more.
  • Trims hold: extending or trimming a clip edge now sticks exactly where you release it. Your frame decision outranks every automatic rule; reclaimed audio no longer snaps back.
  • Smoother while playing: transcript scrolling during playback no longer lags or jumps, the follow-along highlight keeps tracking through hand-edited sections, and waveforms draw to the very end of every clip at high zoom.

item.title: PowerCut 0.8.3
item.description:
• Selecting text is instant: drag-selecting words and sentences now tracks the cursor with no delay on any project size, and a drag always selects, even when it starts in the margin or between paragraphs.
  • The Strike bar meets your cursor: it appears the moment a drag starts selecting, follows just above the cursor, and lands where you release. Its buttons only accept clicks once the mouse is up.

item.title: PowerCut 0.8.2
item.description:
• Projects open instantly: the audio analysis now travels with the project file, so reopening no longer re-reads every clip's audio. Cards land settled, waveforms already drawn. A clip whose media changed on disk re-analyzes automatically.
  • Switching audio tracks remembers everything: the transcript and every edit on the track you leave (strikes, corrections, take picks) come back instantly when you switch back, no re-transcription, and it survives closing the project.
  • Audio tracks show their recorded names ("Lav", "Mix L") in the dropdowns and on the clip card instead of bare numbers.

item.title: PowerCut 0.8.1
item.description:
• Take the tour: a guided quick start for new users, twelve short steps that ride your own first project, from dropping in footage to export. Each step points at the real control, advances as you do the real thing, and can be skipped at any moment. Replay it any time from Help > Take the Tour.
  • The tour never blocks the app (everything stays clickable while a bubble is up), Back and Skip are always available, and existing users are not interrupted: the welcome only appears on a truly first launch.

item.title: PowerCut 0.8.0
item.description:
• Assistant Editor + (beta): completely optional, and PowerCut works fully without it. Connect your own Claude or ChatGPT API key in Settings and four assistant actions appear in the editor: Seam Lint reads the cut for seams that don't flow and can restore clipped words, Best Takes double-checks take picks against your script, Story Assembly proposes the strongest order, Transcript Polish fixes misheard words.
  • Nothing applies without you: every suggestion lands in a review sheet with its reason and confidence, accepted changes apply as one undoable step, and a safety Version is saved first. Only the transcript and PowerCut's measurements are sent, never audio, video, or files, and only when you press an action. Your key lives in the macOS Keychain and usage bills to your own provider account, typically cents per run.

item.title: PowerCut 0.7.9
item.description:
• Every clip card now shows its edit: "Cut 2:58 · saves 1:31" under the cut count, live with every edit, in the same language as the timeline strip. Durations read as a clear T: 00:00:00 timecode, and audio details moved onto the Audio row, now shown for every clip with audio.
  • The Delete key works everywhere, reliably: strike a selection, press again on struck material to bring it back, exactly like S. In the Document view, Delete acts on the word you last clicked. A keyboard-handling fix stops the key from occasionally bouncing with an error sound.

item.title: PowerCut 0.7.8
item.description:
• Cleaner cuts around struck material: the pause next to a crossed-out take now belongs to the cut, so the first syllable of rejected takes can no longer sneak into the edit. Padding still applies off the kept words; it just never re-exposes removed audio.
  • Delete does what you expect: strike a selection, press again on struck material to bring it back, and now a single word at the caret toggles too, exactly like S. Paragraph-start merge is unchanged.

item.title: PowerCut 0.7.7
item.description:
• Shared projects find their media: open a .powercuts file and media sitting next to it links up automatically, verified against the clip's stored metadata. Zip the project folder, send it, it opens working.
  • Relink Media: a new dialog lists every offline clip with its own Locate button (external drives welcome) plus Match a Folder for the batch case. Clips you can't find keep their entire edit and keep working from saved data.
  • Choose the automatic first pass before it runs: the new-project screen shows the cleanup options (fillers, takes, asides, context judgment) so a plain transcript with pause cuts only is one click away. Choices are remembered for the next project.
  • Undo reliably wins against relinking still in progress, and an interrupted relink can never save the wrong file into your project.

item.title: PowerCut 0.7.6
item.description:
• Auto Detect for mixed-language clips, in beta: Whisper re-detects the spoken language about every 30 seconds and writes each part in its own script. One clip, several languages, one transcript. Find it at the bottom of every language menu.
  • One export dialog for transcripts and captions: choose the full record, cuts struck through, or the video edit only, then deliver it in the original languages or translated to English. The translation happens at export time; your project and edit are never changed, strikes map onto the English words by time, and results are cached so repeat exports are instant.
  • English captions for foreign-language edits: the same language choice applies to the .srt export, so a Hindi edit ships with English captions in one step.
  • The export dialog calls out clips that have no transcript yet instead of leaving them silently missing.

item.title: PowerCut 0.7.5
item.description:
• Translate to English, in beta: Whisper listens to the spoken language and writes the transcript in English, every word timed to the original footage, so cuts land exactly where things were said. Per clip from any language menu, or the whole project from the Translate button. Pick the language or let Auto Detect handle it.
  • Your edit survives translation: strikes and cuts stay where they are in the footage, mapped by time onto the English words, or run the Auto Edit Pass fresh. Nothing is touched until the translation actually succeeds, so a failed download or an offline moment loses nothing.
  • New Transcription Accuracy setting: Standard, or Maximum with OpenAI's full Large-v3 model, noticeably more accurate on Hindi and translation (about a 3 GB one-time download). In Settings, the settings column, and the Translate dialog.
  • English scripts now guide take picking on translated footage, and Hinglish is available as a translation source.
  • Sturdier transcription pipeline ordering and more robust undo around in-flight background work.

item.title: PowerCut 0.7.4
item.description:
• New Document view: your transcript as a clean paper page. Serif type, margin timestamps, clip headings, whole-document zoom. Read-only preview by default with click-to-play on every word; press Edit Document for full editing: strike, restore, correct, and move material right on the page.
  • A follow-along cursor tracks the playhead word by word while the video plays, and the page scrolls with it. Clicking a clip in the footage column jumps the document to that section.
  • See the cut your way: Strike Thru Cuts shows the full transcript with cut material struck through, plain text with it off, or Hide Cuts for a clean read. With the full transcript showing, playback switches to full footage so every line plays, cut or kept.
  • Word document export in three flavors: the full uncut record, the edited transcript with real strikethrough, or only what made the video edit. Also in the File menu with XML and caption export.
  • Footage column: select several clips with Cmd or Shift click and remove them together; one undo brings them all back.
  • Faster document scrolling on long projects, button labels that survive smaller windows, a tinted highlight on moved material, and safer Word export that never overwrites a file until the new one is complete.

item.title: PowerCut 0.7.3
item.description:
• Two more languages, in beta: Hindi and Hinglish, carried by a new on-device Whisper engine. Thirteen languages total. The Whisper model downloads once on first use (about 1.5 GB) and everything stays on your Mac.
  • Fixed a freeze when importing very large batches of clips at once. Drop in 44 clips; they now flow through in seconds instead of hanging the app.
  • Devanagari sentence marks (danda) are understood by the pacing engine.

item.title: PowerCut 0.7.2
item.description:
• Try styles without losing work: switching Video Style saves your current edit to Versions first and asks what you want, re-tune the timing only, or also re-run the Auto Edit Pass for the new feel. Come back to a style you edited under before and PowerCut offers that edit back, exactly as you left it.
  • Every video style now explains itself: a caption under the picker describes what the selected style does to pacing and pauses.

item.title: PowerCut 0.7.1
item.description:
• Five more languages, in beta: Japanese with the full pipeline (filler and stutter detection included), plus Korean, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional) and Cantonese with transcription, pause cuts and the whole paper edit. Pick per project or per clip; each clip card now has a language dropdown.
  • Hide Cuts (formerly Struck) now gives a truly clean read: struck text collapses behind faint marks, fully struck passages fold into a single line, and the timeline switches to the edited view. The timeline's own Hide Cuts toggle stays independent.
  • Stray single-word edits between cuts (a marooned "So" making a half-second clip) are struck automatically. Restorable like every automatic strike, and it learns from your restores.
  • Tooltips across the whole interface, and a crash fix when hiding struck text.

item.title: PowerCut 0.7.0
item.description:
• Six languages: transcribe projects in English, Spanish, French, German, Italian or Portuguese. Pick the main language on the start page, or set a language per clip from the sidebar. Models download once, on first use.
  • Transcript scrolling is dramatically smoother on long projects.
  • Exports are frame-exact: adjacent cuts tile precisely, with no one-frame drift.
  • Multi-track audio extraction streams to disk, so very long recordings no longer spike memory.
  • Switching a clip's audio track or language mid-analysis can no longer mix results from the old run.

item.title: PowerCut 0.6.2
item.description:
• Find in transcript (⌘F): search every clip for words or phrases, close matches included, with a results list showing timecode, clip and match percentage. Matches highlight in the transcript.
  • Corrections at scale: fix a mis-heard word everywhere in the project in one step, and optionally remember it for every future transcript. Every automatic correction now shows a teal underline with what was heard, and right-click reverts it.
  • Keyboard fixes: typing in any text field never triggers shortcuts, S now strikes or restores in one key, and word corrections have a Cancel button.
  • Window resizing is smooth, and PowerCut wears its new icon.

item.title: PowerCut 0.6.1
item.description:
• Missing footage is now handled the way an editor would want. If a drive is unplugged or a file moves, the clip stays in your project marked in red, with the transcript and every edit intact. Playback holds its place, and you keep editing from the saved data.
  • Exports still include offline clips, referencing the original files, so Final Cut, Resolve and Premiere show them as offline media and relink the moment the files are back.
  • Plug the drive back in and everything heals automatically. Files that moved: right-click the clip and choose Locate Missing File.

item.title: PowerCut 0.6.0
item.description:
• MXF import. Sony, Canon and Panasonic broadcast files drop straight into PowerCut: transcribe, edit and export like any other clip. Camera timecode and every audio track come along.
  • Exports still reference your original MXF files, untouched, so Final Cut, Resolve and Premiere relink to the camera originals.
  • Powered by a bundled FFmpeg helper (LGPL) that repackages MXF losslessly where macOS allows, with a fast preview fallback where it doesn't. Audio is always untouched.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.10
item.description: • Fixes a crash at launch when the last project's footage can't be found (for example, an unplugged external drive). PowerCut now opens normally and lists the missing files instead.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.9
item.description:
• Recent Projects in the File menu: your last ten projects, one click to reopen. The current edit always autosaves before switching.
  • Projects without a name now autosave as Untitled_01, Untitled_02 and so on, and follow along when you give them a real name. No more hunting for an edit you forgot to name.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.8
item.description:
• Camera timecode handled per camera and per NLE: DJI (and any camera writing a real timecode track) lines up at source timecode in Final Cut, Resolve and Premiere.
  • Sony footage exports import cleanly into Final Cut Pro again (no more "invalid edit" warnings), while Resolve keeps the timecode form it needs to link Sony files.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.7
item.description:
• Clips in the sidebar can be dragged to reorder again: the card lifts, the others move apart as you go, and one Undo covers the whole move.
  • The clip count now reads "2 of 5 on" when some clips are switched off.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.6
item.description:
• After the free trial, PowerCut now stays fully usable: editing, transcription and the auto pass all keep working, and only export needs a license. The trial-end screen no longer locks the whole app.
  • Enter License sits right beside Unlock, so a purchased key is never a hunt.
  • Add Footage moved to the top of the sidebar, under the project name.
  • Named projects export to Final Cut Pro with the event and timeline under exactly that name.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.5
item.description:
• Final Cut Pro import fixed for Sony camera footage: multicam exports no longer trigger "Invalid edit with no respective media." Resolve exports keep their timecode-based form.
  • Timeline trimming is now frame-accurate, like trimming in Final Cut Pro: the edge stays exactly where you release it instead of snapping back.
  • Transcript words strike or restore only when the trim covers or reveals the whole word - shaving frames off a word edits the audio without changing the text.
  • Dragging a trim out and back in now behaves chronologically: the latest drag always wins.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.4
item.description:
• Sony camera timecode is now written into Final Cut and Resolve exports, so DaVinci Resolve links FX3 and other Sony MP4 clips correctly.
  • Cut padding now applies to every cut, including removed takes and filler words, and the sliders update the edit reliably.
  • Words at the end of a sentence are no longer clipped when the next take is removed.
  • Striking and restoring words is much faster, and rapid edits no longer stall playback.
  • Reset buttons on the Pauses and Cut Padding panels.
  • Footage Brief highlights clear when you click elsewhere, and the auto pass shows its progress while it runs.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.3
item.description:
PowerCut 0.5.3

  • Final Cut Pro imports without warnings. Exports now carry the format names Final Cut expects, so it no longer reports an unexpected value on the timeline or on multicam clips.
  • Better timeline size. The project is built on a standard Final Cut format chosen from the footage the cut is actually made of, rather than inheriting an odd capture size from whichever clip happened to be first. A screen recording in your story no longer sets the resolution for the whole project.
  • Multicam exports import cleanly, following on from the multicam fix in 0.5.2.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.2
item.description:
PowerCut 0.5.2

  • Final Cut Pro multicam export fixed. The multicam option wrote a file Final Cut rejected without an error, so nothing appeared on import.
  • Cuts land where they should. Edit points are now found in the audio itself rather than from transcript timings, so clips start right before the first word and end after the last one finishes, with no chopped words and no dead air at the head.
  • Breaths and long pauses removed between sentences, with the padding sliders genuinely controlling how the edit breathes.
  • Much stronger repeat and false start detection: re-read lines are matched against your script, restarts buried inside a sentence are caught, and mis-transcribed repeats no longer slip through.
  • Run Auto Edit Pass now re-derives cleanly instead of layering on the previous pass, so improved detection applies to projects you already started.
  • Click a word to play from it. Clicking selects the word and starts playback at that moment.
  • New Project in the File menu, and Previous Projects on the name pill.
  • Smoother settings sliders with a confirmation before re-planning, a larger selection popup, and panels that stay usable at small window sizes.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.1
item.description:
PowerCut 0.5.1

  • New transcript click model: click places the caret, double-click selects a word, triple-click selects a paragraph. Delete toggles strike and restore.
  • Playback speeds now go to 2x, with a compact speed menu next to the timeline play button.
  • Previous Projects dropdown on the project name pill, listing your five most recent projects.
  • Granular audio selection: pick the left or right channel of any track for transcription, right from the clip's context menu.
  • Larger default transcript text with a numeric size indicator.
  • Hover a clip to remove it, a visible audio track chip, and an optional auto-transcribe on import setting.
  • Many smaller fixes from tester feedback.

item.title: PowerCut 0.5.0
item.description:
PowerCut 0.5.0

First test build: on-device transcription and rough cuts, paper editing, the Auto Edit Pass, take detection, the review queue, versions, and export to Final Cut Pro, DaVinci Resolve and Premiere Pro plus captions.
